correctness.rationale: For L=U⊕W⊕(U⊗W) with central Z and [u+w,u'+w']=u⊗w'−u'⊗w, an ideal I is exactly specified by X=projection in U⊕W, C=I∩Z with [X,U⊕W]⊆C, and a linear graph lift X→Z/C. If projections A⊆U and B⊆W have dimensions r,s, Goursat graph classification of X uses quotient dimension k and dim X=r+s−k, counted by [a r]_q[b s]_q[r k]_q[s k]_q |GL_k(Fq)|. The bracket image is A⊗W+U⊗B, with central quotient dimension c=(a−r)(b−s); choose t-dimensional central subspace [c t]_q then q^{(r+s−k)(c−t)} graph lifts. Ideal dimension is ab−c+t+r+s−k. All are bijective including char2 due to alternating bracket. Independently evaluated full 4-index formula at (a,b,q)=(1,1,2),(1,1,3),(1,2,2),(1,2,3),(2,2,2), giving ideal totals 6,7,26,45,247. Also independently enumerated all 374 subspaces of 5-dimensional F2^5 for (1,2,2) and tested bracket closure; dimension coefficients {0:1,1:3,2:7,3:7,4:7,5:1}, total26, matching formula. This supports, but does not replace, the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The complete-bipartite Lie family is natural and its all-ideal dimension generating polynomial is not the restricted subgraph-derived ideal data in Godoy Molina–Lagos, nor the general subspace-checking algorithm in Lee's 2020 finite-field zeta-function framework. Lee's primary Theorem 2.6 includes the a=b=1 3D Heisenberg case, which is explicitly excluded from novelty; it does not contain the uniform arbitrary a,b fourfold polynomial. Broader finite-dimensional/zeta-function theory requires nontrivial projection and lifting enumeration to derive this family-specific closed answer.

A uniform q-polynomial giving the entire ideal dimension profile across all a,b is a natural complete enumeration useful in Lie ideal-counting/zeta-function theory; not merely a known scalar Heisenberg result or a table recomputation.
